items.name: Capri-Sun
clues: Bright, sunny and a bit childish. It's what was in your school bag on a hot day.
Thin layers of plastic and aluminium, opened with a straw. EU rules on single-use plastic turned the straw into paper in 2021.
Launched in Germany in 1969 by a flavour company from Heidelberg. In the late 1970s, a world-famous boxer appeared in its adverts.
A little silver bag that stands up on its own.
The battle to push the straw through the tiny hole without spraying juice everywhere. In 2024 its boss said paper straws annoy many customers.
German speakers grew up with its old name, Capri-Sonne.

items.name: Toblerone
clues: Swiss, proud and a bit pointy. It's what people buy at the airport at the very last minute.
Milk chocolate with honey and almond nougat, in a cardboard box.
Created in Bern in 1908. In 2023 part of its production moved to Slovakia, so under Swiss rules it had to remove a famous picture from its pack.
A long triangle that never fits flat in your bag, and the bar inside is a row of little peaks.
A Swiss mountain on the old box, with a bear hidden in it. In 2016 British fans were furious when the gaps between the peaks got wider.
Its name joins the founder's surname, Tobler, to torrone, the Italian word for nougat.

items.name: Tetra Pak
clues: Practical and almost invisible: you've held one thousands of times without thinking about its name.
Mostly paperboard, with very thin layers of plastic and aluminium inside, so recyclers have to separate the layers.
A Swedish company from Lund, founded in 1951. Its first pack, in 1952, was for cream.
The first ones had four triangular sides, like a pyramid. Later came a famous brick shape.
In German supermarkets, a lot of the milk, juice and oat drinks come in its cartons.
Its name starts with the Greek word for 'four', after that first four-sided shape.

items.name: PEZ
clues: Cheerful and collectable: half sweet, half toy.
Small hard sweets in a paper wrapper, which you load into a plastic dispenser.
Invented in Vienna in 1927 as a peppermint for adults, sold as an alternative to smoking.
The first dispensers looked like a cigarette lighter. You tip the top back and one sweet slides out.
From 1955 the dispensers got heads, like Santa Claus, Popeye and Mickey Mouse, and people now collect them.
Its three-letter name comes from the German word PfeffErminZ.

items.name: Nespresso
clues: Elegant, a bit posh and very pleased with itself. It wants your kitchen to feel like a boutique.
Small aluminium capsules, which critics say create a mountain of waste for one cup of coffee.
A Swiss food giant launched it in 1986.
A tiny metal cup with a sealed lid that you drop into a machine.
A Hollywood actor has starred in its adverts since 2006, with the line 'What else?'
Its name joins the company that owns it, Nestlé, to a short, strong Italian coffee.

items.name: Tupperware
clues: Practical and a bit old-fashioned: the thing your parents fill with leftovers and never give back.
Strong, reusable plastic with a lid that seals.
An American inventor started the company in 1946. It became famous for selling at home parties instead of in shops, and in 2024 it filed for bankruptcy.
Boxes and bowls in every size, often in bright colours, that stack inside each other.
You press the middle of the lid to let the air out, and it makes a little 'burp'.
Germans often just say 'eine Tupperdose', using its first syllable.
